commonMistakes: Putting units in the variable and again outside it (e.g. var(--space)px) incorrectly.
beginnerTips: You can nest var() and use variables inside calc().
topics.title: var()

topics.description: :root is the document element — the usual place for global design tokens. Changing a token updates every consumer. This reference site uses tokens for colors and spacing so themes stay consistent.
topics.whenToUse: Global theme values shared across the whole site.
topics.whenNotToUse: Component-private values that should not leak globally — scope them on a parent class.
commonMistakes: Defining conflicting globals and overriding with !important instead of scoping.
beginnerTips: Group tokens: color, space, font, radius sections in your stylesheet.
topics.title: :root variables

subsections.title: Responsive Design
subsections.description: Layouts that adapt to screen size.

topics.description: Media queries apply CSS only when a condition matches — usually viewport width, but also preferences like prefers-reduced-motion. Use them to adapt layout, typography, and navigation. Prefer fewer, meaningful breakpoints over tiny one-off tweaks.
topics.whenToUse: Adapting styles across viewport sizes and user preferences.
topics.whenNotToUse: When fluid units, flex, or auto-fit grid already solve the problem without a query.
commonMistakes: Dozens of breakpoints that fight each other and are hard to maintain.
beginnerTips: Test by resizing the browser; do not assume one phone width covers all cases.
topics.title: Media queries

topics.summary: Write base styles for small screens, then add complexity with min-width queries.
topics.description: Mobile-first means the default CSS works on phones. Then @media (min-width: …) enhances for larger screens. This avoids fighting desktop-only assumptions and keeps the base layer simple. Start with stacked layout, then add columns as space allows.
topics.whenToUse: Most modern responsive projects.
topics.whenNotToUse: Rare fixed-size kiosk UIs that never change width.
commonMistakes: Designing only on a wide monitor, then bolting on fragile max-width patches for mobile.
beginnerTips: Write the small-screen layout without queries first, then layer min-width enhancements.
Prefer min-width queries over a thicket of max-width overrides.
topics.title: Mobile-first design

topics.summary: %, em, rem, vw, vh, and more.
topics.description: Different units scale differently: % relative to a parent, rem to the root font size, vw/vh to the viewport. Choose based on what should scale. Mixing units is normal — borders in px, type in rem, columns in fr.
topics.whenToUse: Picking units intentionally for type, spacing, and layout.
topics.whenNotToUse: Using vw for everything — text can become unreadable or ignore user font settings.
commonMistakes: Viewport-only type that ignores browser default font size preferences.
beginnerTips: rem for type/spacing systems; %/fr for flexible layout widths.
topics.title: Responsive units overview

topics.description: vw and vh are percentages of the viewport width and height. 100vh is a common full-screen section height, but mobile browser chrome can make it awkward. 100vw can include scrollbar quirks — test carefully.
topics.whenToUse: Viewport-relative hero sizing and large proportional UI.
topics.whenNotToUse: Body text sizing solely in vw without clamp limits.
commonMistakes: 100vw causing horizontal scroll because scrollbars add extra width.
beginnerTips: Prefer min-height: 100dvh when you need modern dynamic viewport behavior.
topics.title: vw & vh

topics.description: Percentage sizes are relative to the parent’s corresponding measure. Percentage height only works if the parent has an explicit height. Width percentages are the backbone of fluid layouts inside fixed or flexible parents.
topics.whenToUse: Fluid widths inside a sized parent container.
topics.whenNotToUse: Height: 100% chains without defined parent heights — they often fail.
commonMistakes: Assuming % height resolves against the viewport — it resolves against the parent.
beginnerTips: If height % fails, check every ancestor for a defined height.
topics.title: % sizes

topics.summary: rem = root font size; em = relative to parent font size.
topics.description: rem is relative to the root element’s font size and stays predictable in nested components. em is relative to the parent’s font size and can compound. Prefer rem for spacing systems; use em when scaling with local text size (e.g. button padding).
topics.whenToUse: Scalable type and spacing that respects root font size.
topics.whenNotToUse: Deeply nested em font sizes that compound into chaos.
commonMistakes: Nesting em font-size three levels deep and getting microscopic or huge text.
beginnerTips: Many design systems define spacing as rem multiples of 4px/8px.
topics.title: rem & em

topics.summary: CSS pixels — stable but less fluid alone.
topics.description: px are CSS pixels — stable and precise. Still useful for borders, hairlines, and fine UI chrome. For typography and large layout widths, rem/%/fr usually adapt better. Users can still zoom pages with px type.
topics.whenToUse: Borders, shadows, icons, and precise chrome.
topics.whenNotToUse: Entire page layouts locked to fixed px widths that break on small screens.
commonMistakes: Fixed 1200px content wrappers with no max-width: 100% for mobile.
beginnerTips: 1px borders remain a common, sensible use of px.
topics.title: px

topics.description: clamp(min, preferred, max) picks a value within bounds — excellent for fluid typography and spacing. The preferred value often mixes rem and vw. You get smooth scaling without many breakpoints.
topics.whenToUse: Fluid type, padding, and widths that need floors and ceilings.
topics.whenNotToUse: Simple fixed sizes where a single rem value is clearer.
commonMistakes: Preferred values that ignore the min/max and look wrong at mid widths — test the range.
beginnerTips: Always set a readable min and max so text never becomes tiny or huge.
topics.title: clamp()

topics.summary: auto-fit + minmax builds fluid card grids.
topics.description: Responsive grids often use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) so columns reflow as space allows. This reduces media-query clutter for card galleries. Tune the minimum track size until cards feel good on phones and desktops.
topics.whenToUse: Card grids and galleries that should reflow automatically.
topics.whenNotToUse: Strict editorial layouts that need exact column counts per breakpoint.
commonMistakes: Mixing auto-fit grids with conflicting fixed widths on children.
beginnerTips: Raise the minmax minimum if cards feel too narrow on large screens with many columns.
topics.title: Responsive grids

topics.summary: Scale type with clamp and comfortable line lengths.
topics.description: Responsive typography scales type with clamp and keeps line length readable (often about 45–75 characters on desktop). Pair font-size with line-height and max-width. Do not scale type so aggressively that mobile becomes tiny or desktop becomes shouty.
topics.whenToUse: Comfortable reading experiences across devices.
topics.whenNotToUse: Forcing one giant heading size everywhere without a max clamp.

files.code: Readable fluid paragraph text that adjusts within a minimum and maximum size.

commonMistakes: Fluid type without a max, producing enormous headlines on wide monitors.
beginnerTips: max-width on paragraphs helps as much as fluid font-size.
topics.title: Responsive typography

topics.description: calc() lets you mix units: width: calc(100% - 2rem). Useful for full-bleed layouts with fixed padding, sticky sidebars, and precise offsets. Spaces around + and - operators are required.
topics.whenToUse: Combining fluid and fixed sizes in one value.
topics.whenNotToUse: Simple values that need no math — a plain length is clearer.
commonMistakes: Writing calc(100%-2rem) without spaces and getting an invalid value.
beginnerTips: Always put spaces around + and - inside calc().
topics.title: calc()

topics.description: min() picks the smaller value; max() picks the larger. Related to clamp(), which uses both a floor and a ceiling. width: min(100%, 220px) caps a box while allowing it to shrink on small screens.
topics.whenToUse: Caps and floors without full clamp() when you only need one bound.
topics.whenNotToUse: When you need both min and max — use clamp() instead.
commonMistakes: Swapping min and max and getting the opposite constraint you intended.
beginnerTips: min(100%, 40rem) is a classic readable measure pattern for text containers.
topics.title: min() & max()

topics.description: aspect-ratio preserves a width/height relationship such as 16/9. Great for video placeholders, thumbnails, and cards. Prefer it over old padding-top hacks. The box still responds to width constraints.
topics.whenToUse: Media frames, maps, and boxes that must keep a ratio.
topics.whenNotToUse: Containers whose height should always follow variable content instead.
commonMistakes: Also setting a conflicting fixed height that fights the ratio.
beginnerTips: Set width (or max-width) and let aspect-ratio compute height.
topics.title: aspect-ratio

topics.summary: How replaced content fills its box.
topics.description: object-fit controls how replaced content (,
topics.whenToUse: Images and videos inside fixed frames that must crop or fit consistently.
topics.whenNotToUse: Background decoration — background-size may be more appropriate.
commonMistakes: Expecting object-fit to work without setting width/height (or equivalent).
beginnerTips: object-fit only applies when the element has a definite box size.
topics.title: object-fit & position

topics.description: overflow controls clipping and scrollbars: visible, hidden, auto, or scroll. auto shows scrollbars when needed; hidden clips. overflow: hidden can also break position: sticky on descendants — know the tradeoff.
topics.whenToUse: Scrollable panels, clipping decorative overflow, and modal bodies.
topics.whenNotToUse: Hiding content users need without another way to reach it.

files.code: Overflowing content that should scroll inside this small box when needed.

commonMistakes: overflow: hidden on a parent accidentally killing sticky headers inside.
beginnerTips: overflow-x and overflow-y can be set independently.
topics.title: overflow

topics.description: filter applies visual effects like blur, grayscale, and brightness to an element’s rendering. Filters can create new stacking contexts and affect performance on large areas. Prefer subtle effects for UI; heavier effects for images.
topics.whenToUse: Image treatments and light UI emphasis effects.
topics.whenNotToUse: Blurring entire pages as a substitute for proper disabled/loading states.
commonMistakes: Heavy blur on huge layers causing jank on low-end devices.
beginnerTips: Space-separated functions combine: blur(4px) brightness(1.1).
topics.title: filter

topics.description: opacity sets whole-element transparency including children and text. Values range from 0 to 1. For fading only a background, prefer a color with alpha. opacity less than 1 also creates a stacking context.
topics.whenToUse: Fading entire elements for disabled or transitional states.
topics.whenNotToUse: Fading only the background while keeping text crisp — use rgba/hsla instead.
commonMistakes: Using opacity on a wrapper and unintentionally fading nested buttons/text.
beginnerTips: Animate opacity for smooth fades; it is GPU-friendly with transform.
topics.title: opacity

topics.summary: translate, rotate, scale, skew — without reflowing layout like margin hacks.
topics.description: transform moves, rotates, scales, or skews visually without reflowing document layout the way margins would. Ideal with transitions for hover lifts and motion. Transformed elements create a containing block for fixed descendants in many cases — test overlays carefully.
topics.whenToUse: Visual motion, hover lifts, and rotational accents.
topics.whenNotToUse: Actual document flow spacing — transforms do not push siblings away.
commonMistakes: Using transform for layout gaps and wondering why space collapses for siblings.
beginnerTips: Prefer transform: translateY(-4px) over relative top for animated lifts.
topics.title: transforms

topics.summary: Modern browsers support nesting rules inside rules.
topics.description: Native nesting lets you write .card { .title { } &:hover { } } similar to Sass. Support is strong in current browsers — confirm for your audience. Nesting improves locality but deep nests can hurt readability and raise specificity. Keep nests shallow and intentional.
topics.whenToUse: Component-scoped styles in modern codebases.
topics.whenNotToUse: If you must support very old browsers without a build step.
commonMistakes: Nesting so deep that selectors become brittle and hard to override.
beginnerTips: Nest hover/focus states under the component, not three levels deeper than needed.
Use & for the parent selector when appending pseudo-classes.
topics.title: Native CSS nesting
